method.3.4-storage-order: structural/order/storage_order_scan.py: a copy of tools/storage_order_check.py (unchanged there) extended with rules prefix-split (TOP/LIMIT assembled from several literals, f-string placeholders resolved from the function's assignments), first-row (fetchone()/fetchall()[0] of an unordered multi-row SELECT), os-first-row (&sql SELECT INTO outside a cursor; dynamic statements read with one If rs.%Next()), os-cursor-alloc (a result-set loop without ORDER BY that allocates identities), os-cutoff (Quit:/If count cut-offs over a cursor or $Order), py-slice-cut (a slice of an unordered fetched list or a set); scope iris_vector_graph, api, src (.py) and iris_src/src, src (.cls); sites mapped to modules via models/breadth-c/inventory.json (innermost entry range, else file owners), overridden per site by the disposition's module where the inventory names several. Automatic classes from the statement text: ORDER BY present (incl. an ORDER BY in the same f-string or the assembled statement), existence (TOP 1 1, WHERE 1=0, TOP 0, fetchone() is (not) None), single-row aggregate, unique key (WHERE pins every column of a declared key, schema.py DDL keys), collation order ($Order loops). Every other site of the gated modules has a hand disposition (dispositions.json, made by make_dispositions.py) with path:line cites and an anchor text that must occur within 3 lines of the site; the gate fails on an undisposed site, a stale cite or anchor, an unknown class or an unused disposition.
method.3.6-row-permutation: structural/order/permutation.py: per module a small dataset written through the product's writers in three insertion orders (forward, reverse, fixed shuffle), AUDITD emptied by lib.reset (Eraser.EraseAll, Ledger.PurgeAll) between orders inside one lock hold; the module's read APIs compared across orders: set (deep multiset), list (exact, where the contract has an order or a top-k/paging cut) or sample (may differ; every answer must pass a well-formedness validator). Generated ids, digests, seqs and blank nodes normalised where they follow an explicit order by design; statement ids kept where they are the subject (F-C1108). Per-module verdicts (verdict.py) are registered separately so a module's cell cites only its own result. so_live.py confirms the storage-order reliance sites live (two insertion orders).
